transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I guess what brought me in is that I just can't keep my mind on one thing anymore. 

It's really affecting my work. I'll be in the middle of fixing a rendering bug, and... a Slack ping, or maybe a certain color pattern on the screen, or even just a siren outside will happen, and it pulls me into a completely new idea before I can even finish typing the line of code. I just keep getting pulled away.
Do you often feel like you have an internal motor that keeps you moving, or do you find it difficult to sit still for long periods?

Yeah, I definitely feel that way. It's like I've been running on this constant current lately. I mean, I wake up and my brain is already going—I'm planning out new features, thinking about exhibition layouts, figuring out press angles, and making code changes. Sitting still just feels like... well, it feels like I'm wasting the moment. I just have to keep moving.
Has this feeling of being constantly driven and needing to keep moving been your typical state for as long as you can remember, or is this a shift from how you usually feel?

No, it's definitely a shift. I haven't always been like this. I'd say... well, it's been going on for about three months now. It really started right after my platform was selected for the Glendale showcase.
During the last few months, have you also experienced any periods where you felt persistently sad, hopeless, or completely uninterested in things you usually enjoy?

No, not really. I mean, I haven't felt sad or down at all. If anything, it's the exact opposite. I haven't had any moments where I felt hopeless or lost interest in my work or anything else. I've just been incredibly focused on getting everything ready for the showcase.
During these past three months, have you ever felt that you were receiving special messages or that you had abilities or insights that others around you didn't seem to have?

Well, I wouldn't call them special messages exactly, but... I do know things that other people haven't picked up on yet. I'm absolutely sure that some of the major museums, and probably a couple of big investors, are quietly circling my platform. 

It's just obvious if you look at the details. The language they used for the showcase announcement, the timing of their Instagram posts, even some random emails I've been getting at work... they all line up way too perfectly to just be a coincidence. They're definitely watching what I'm doing.

Looking back at your life before these last three months, have you ever experienced a period of at least two weeks where you felt significantly depressed, hopeless, or lost interest in almost all of your usual activities?

No, I can't say that I have. I've never really been a depressed kind of person. I mean, sure, I've had bad days or weeks where work was stressful, but I've never felt hopeless or just stopped caring about my life or my projects for weeks at a time. That's just not me.

Do you feel that these museums and investors are watching you because of your special abilities or the unique success of your project, or do you believe they have been following you or tracking you for other reasons that have nothing to do with your work?

No, it's... it's definitely because of the project. I mean, I don't think they care about my personal life or anything like that. It's strictly about what I've built. 

The platform is just that good, and they want to get in on it before it officially launches. So, yeah, it's all about the work. There's no other reason they'd be paying this much attention to me, it's just business.
Before these past three months, have you ever had any other periods in your life where you felt this same high energy, racing thoughts, or need for less sleep than usual?

No, I really haven't. This is... well, it's the first time I've ever felt quite like this. I've always been pretty focused on my work, but I've never had this kind of constant energy or gone this long without needing much sleep before. It's just been these last few months.
Have these feelings and thoughts about the investors and museums been constant every single day for the entire three-month period?

Yeah, I'd say they've been pretty constant lately, but... well, not for the whole three months. I mean, before this whole showcase push really ramped up, I wasn't reading secret messages from museums or investors into posts and emails. That stuff... it really only started after I got so energized and completely consumed by the project. Once I stopped sleeping as much and got really dialed in, that's when I started noticing all the signs.

Has your current level of energy and focus caused you to make any impulsive decisions or take any risks that have resulted in significant negative consequences for your personal life, finances, or professional reputation?

Well, I guess... yeah, there have been some issues. I ended up spending money that my business partner and I hadn't agreed on. I bought a bunch of GPUs, got high-end print materials made, and paid for promo videos. I just felt like we had to move fast. And... I also pushed a major update to the platform without getting approval. Waiting for another review cycle just felt like letting the whole opportunity die. My partner was pretty upset about all of it.
